mainTopic: Whether the משנה about combining the shades of נגעים follows רבי עקיבא, and where we learn that רבי עקיבא ranks the shades "זו למעלה מזו"
overview: The גמרא first finishes an earlier discussion. The problem of קרום ביצה can be solved from the פסוק "ולשאת ולספחת", but the problem of סיד היכל cannot. So it concludes that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא. Then it asks where we learn that רבי עקיבא ranks the shades "זו למעלה מזו". It first tries a ברייתא in which יהושע, the son of רבי עקיבא, asks his father why the חכמים named four shades of נגעים. Since יהושע suggested only one rule, 'from קרום ביצה and up', the גמרא infers that רבי עקיבא holds all the shades combine with שאת. But that proof is pushed off: maybe each main shade combines only with its own secondary. Next the גמרא brings רבי חנינא's picture of four cups of milk with more and more drops of blood. This too is challenged. It may fit only reddish (פתוך) shades. Even for those, רבי עקיבא's own description in a משנה in נגעים does not match the cups of milk: the same red sits on a brighter or a duller white.

steps.title: The egg-membrane problem can be solved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the earlier comparison. It grants that the problem of קרום ביצה is solved by the פסוק, because ספחת is secondary to שאת even though it is much lower.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of comparison is this? It would be fine if not for the problem of סיד היכל. The problem of קרום ביצה is not hard. Even though קרום ביצה is lower than שאת, the תורה says "and for the שאת and for the ספחת". That teaches that ספחת is attached to שאת, even though it is much lower than it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rejecting the comparison that was just raised against it. It admits that one of the two problems, קרום ביצה, has a good answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that קרום ביצה is too far below שאת to combine with it. The פסוק "ולשאת ולספחת" shows that ספחת is attached to שאת no matter how far below it is. So distance in brightness does not stop it from combining. This only solves half of the problem, and the next step says so.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it would be fine (admits one point before raising a problem)
Lime plaster of the Sanctuary walls, one of the shades of נגעים
The membrane of an egg, one of the shades of נגעים
One of the main types of צרעת mark named in the תורה
A secondary type of mark, attached to the main type
Secondary / attached to something else

phrases.english: What is this?
phrases.notes: This is a way of saying: what kind of comparison is that? The גמרא is questioning what it just suggested.

phrases.english: Granted, if not for the lime of the Sanctuary,
the egg membrane is not difficult —

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דִּקְרוּם בֵּיצָה מִתַּתַּאי דִּשְׂאֵת,
phrases.english: for even though the egg membrane is below the שאת,
the Merciful One said: "And for the שאת and for the ספחת" —
the ספחת is secondary to the שאת,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִנַּחֲתָא מִינַּיהּ טוּבָא.
phrases.english: even though it is much lower than it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּלָא סִיד הֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about whether the משנה can follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison. It grants that the קרום ביצה problem is answered, but sets up that the סיד היכל problem is not.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only one of the two problems can be solved, so the comparison does not fully work.
steps.terutzMaskana: ספחת is attached to שאת even when it is much lower, so קרום ביצה is no problem.

steps.title: The lime problem remains, so the משנה is not like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The problem of סיד היכל has no answer, so the גמרא concludes that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But סיד היכל really is a problem. So it is clear that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the second problem, סיד היכל, cannot be answered. So it decides that our משנה is not following רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of "ולשאת ולספחת" helped only with the shade attached to שאת. It does nothing for סיד היכל. Since that problem stays, the attempt to fit the משנה into רבי עקיבא's view is dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear (the גמרא's final decision after other attempts fail)
Our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Final result of this section: our משנה about combining shades does not follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: But the lime of the Sanctuary — is difficult,
rather, it is clear
that our משנה is not like רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes step 1: one problem was solved, the other was not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Where do we learn רבי עקיבא's ranking of the shades?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that רבי עקיבא ranks the shades one above the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did we learn that רבי עקיבא holds the shades are ranked one above the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the source for רבי עקיבא's view. It is setting up the search for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole discussion depended on רבי עקיבא holding "זו למעלה מזו", that the shades go in order of brightness. Now the גמרא wants to know where that idea actually comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Where did we hear / learn?
This one above that one: the shades ranked in order of brightness

phrases.english: And where did we hear that רבי עקיבא holds
"this one above that one"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After concluding about רבי עקיבא, the גמרא asks for the source of his view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that רבי עקיבא ranks the shades "זו למעלה מזו".

steps.title: A ברייתא: why list four shades?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא as the source. In it, יהושע asks רבי עקיבא why the חכמים called the shades "two that are four", when they could have just said "from egg membrane and up is impure".
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learn it from this ברייתא: רבי יוסי said that יהושע, the son of רבי עקיבא, asked רבי עקיבא: Why did the חכמים say the shades of נגעים are two that are four? רבי עקיבא answered: If not, what should they say? יהושע said: Let them say that anything from קרום ביצה and up is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a ברייתא as a possible source and starts quoting it. The ברייתא opens with a question and answer between רבי עקיבא and his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע's point is that one simple rule would be enough: any mark as bright as קרום ביצה or brighter is impure. So why name four separate shades? The word "אילימא" (if you say) hints that the גמרא may not accept this source in the end.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
The shades of צרעת marks
Two that are four: two main types, each with a secondary shade
Ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: The last line is spoken by יהושע, not by רבי עקיבא, even though the text does not say "he said to him" again before it.

phrases.english: If you say from this — as was taught:
רבי יוסי said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מֵרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: יהושע, son of רבי עקיבא, asked רבי עקיבא:
For what reason did they say
the shades of נגעים are two that are four?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וְאִם לָאו, מָה יֹאמְרוּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: And if not, what should they say?
Let them say: from the egg membrane and up is impure!
phrases.notes: This is the son talking back to his father: just say any mark this bright or brighter is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא ranks the shades "זו למעלה מזו".
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי about יהושע's questions to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: To teach that they combine, and the son's comeback
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the shades were listed to teach that they combine with each other. His son replies that this could also be said in one simple rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: To teach that they combine with each other. יהושע said: Then let them say, "From קרום ביצה and up is impure, and they combine with each other"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a reason for naming the four shades, and his son pushes back again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says the list teaches that the shades combine with each other. יהושע answers that you don't need four names to teach that; you could just add "and they combine" to the simple rule. So the reason for naming each shade is still missing.

keyTerms.meaning: They combine (count together toward the minimum size)
With each other

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: לוֹמַר שֶׁמִּצְטָרְפִים זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.english: He said to him: To say that they combine with each other.
He said to him: Then let them say:
"From the egg membrane and up is impure,
and they combine with each other"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לוֹמַר שֶׁמִּצְטָרְפִים זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation in the ברייתא: an answer followed by another challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shades were listed to teach that they combine with each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reason that the list teaches combining.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Combining could be taught by adding a few words to one simple rule, without naming four shades.

steps.title: A כהן must know the shades and their names
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's final answer: the names are listed to teach that a כהן who is not an expert in the shades and their names may not inspect נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: To tell you that any כהן who is not an expert in them and in their names may not inspect נגעים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his final answer, and the son does not argue back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason for listing each shade by name is practical. A כהן must be able to tell the shades apart and know what each one is called. Without that knowledge he is not allowed to judge נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert / knowledgeable
A priest; only he may declare a נגע impure or pure
Inspects the צרעת marks and rules on them

steps.whatToRemember: The four shades are named so that a כהן must know them and their names before he may judge נגעים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a real requirement: a כהן without expert knowledge of the shades may not inspect נגעים.

phrases.english: He said to him: To tell you,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי בָּהֶן וּבִשְׁמוֹתֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: any כהן who is not an expert in them and in their names
does not inspect the נגעים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לוֹמַר לָךְ, כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא's final answer to his son's repeated challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shades are named so that a כהן must know them and their names in order to inspect נגעים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is not an expert in the shades and their names may not inspect נגעים.

steps.title: Proof from what רבי יהושע left out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע only said 'from egg membrane and up' and never added 'from סיד היכל and up.' So he must have known that רבי עקיבא holds all the shades combine with שאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he did not say 'from lime of the היכל and up.' Since he did not say it, we learn that he had heard רבי עקיבא say that all the shades combine with שאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא from the previous steps carefully and draws a proof from what רבי יהושע did NOT say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose רבי עקיבא held that shades only combine in pairs. Then one rule would not be enough, and רבי יהושע would have needed a second rule: 'from סיד היכל and up.' Since he gave only one rule, he must have known that רבי עקיבא holds all the shades combine with שאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Lime plaster of the היכל, the shade of white just below snow-white
Conclude from it; we learn from this
They combine (count together toward the required size)
Together with

phrases.english: Whereas 'from lime of the Sanctuary and up' —
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע only mentioned egg membrane. If the shades combined just in pairs, he would also need a separate rule starting from the lime shade.

phrases.english: he did not say;
From the fact that he did not say it to him,
conclude from it that he had heard
from Rabbi Akiva that he says:
all of them combine together with a se'et.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of רבי יהושע's suggestion in the ברייתא brought in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא holds all the shades combine with שאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's one-rule suggestion in the ברייתא, which leaves out 'from סיד היכל and up'.

steps.title: Maybe each shade only pairs with its own secondary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe רבי עקיבא holds that שאת combines with its secondary and בהרת combines with its secondary, but nothing more.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he means 'שאת and its secondary' and 'בהרת and its secondary'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 7 and says it does not have to mean what we thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא might still hold the pairs system: שאת with egg membrane, and בהרת with lime. רבי יהושע's 'one rule' could just be a shortened quote that does not tell the whole story. So the silence about סיד היכל proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (opening a rejection)
Its secondary (offspring) shade
The snow-white shade, the brightest main shade

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the pairs. שאת's secondary is egg membrane, and בהרת's secondary is lime of the היכל.

phrases.english: But perhaps 'se'et and its secondary',
'baheret and its secondary'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי יהושע's silence. It does not reject the claim about רבי עקיבא's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can also be read to fit a pairs system (שאת with its secondary, בהרת with its secondary), so it does not prove that all the shades combine with שאת.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's cups of milk analogy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source. רבי חנינא compares רבי עקיבא's view to four cups of milk with 2, 4, 8, and 12 (or 16) drops of blood. All are white, but each is above the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from רבי חנינא, who said: What is רבי עקיבא's view like? Picture four cups of milk. Two drops of blood fell into one, four into another, eight into another, and twelve into the last (some say sixteen). They are all shades of white, but each one is above the other.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first proof, the גמרא brings a different and clearer source for רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The analogy shows four shades that all count as 'white' but form one step-by-step ladder. Each cup is a little less white than the one before. This matches the idea that רבי עקיבא ranks the shades one above the other, which is what the question in step 3 asked for.

keyTerms.meaning: Analogy, comparison
To what is the matter comparable?
This one is above that one (a ranking)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's cups of milk picture four white shades ranked one above the other. Steps 10–12 challenge whether this really tells us רבי עקיבא's view about pure white shades.

phrases.english: Rather, from that of Rabbi Chanina —
as Rabbi Chanina said:
The analogy of Rabbi Akiva's view —
to what is the matter comparable?
To four cups of milk:
one into which fell
two drops of blood,
and one into which fell
four drops of blood,
and one into which fell eight,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד נָפְלוּ לְתוֹכוֹ שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה טִיפִּין –
phrases.english: and one into which fell twelve drops —
and some say: sixteen drops —
for all of them are shades of white,
except that this one is above that one,
and that one is above the next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in step 8 with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא ranks the four shades one above the other in a single chain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's analogy of four cups of milk with more and more drops of blood.

steps.title: Maybe רבי עקיבא only meant reddish-white shades
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from רבי חנינא. His milk-and-blood comparison may only show what רבי עקיבא holds about reddish-white shades (פתוך), not about pure white shades (חלוק).
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that you heard רבי עקיבא say this about shades mixed with red. Did you ever hear him say it about pure white shades?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from רבי חנינא in Step 9. That proof may only cover reddish shades, not pure white ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's picture is milk with drops of blood mixed in. That picture fits shades that are white mixed with red (פתוך). So it proves nothing about the main, pure white shades (חלוק), which are the shades the question was really about.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / perhaps. It opens a possibility that weakens a proof.
Mixed. A white shade blended with red.
Smooth / pure. A plain white shade with no red in it.
Did you hear him say it? A way of saying there is no source for that.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think חלוק means 'divided' here. In נגעים it means a pure, unmixed white, as opposed to פתוך, white mixed with red.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – בְּפָתוּךְ;
phrases.english: Say that you heard רבי עקיבא say this about a mixed (reddish-white) mark;
about pure white, did you hear him say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 9 by narrowing its scope.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רבי חנינא's comparison to reddish-white (פתוך) shades only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The milk-and-blood picture only matches shades mixed with red. It says nothing about pure white shades.

steps.title: Even for reddish shades, did we really hear it?
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say pure white and reddish shades are the same, so what is true for one is true for the other. The גמרא answers that we never even clearly heard this from רבי עקיבא about reddish shades.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: just as you heard it from him about mixed shades, so too you have heard it about pure white shades. But about mixed shades themselves, did you hear it from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone defending the proof by saying both kinds of shades follow the same rule. Then it knocks out that defense, and sets up a source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense is that there is no reason to treat פתוך and חלוק differently. The גמרא does not argue about that. Instead it questions the starting point: maybe רבי עקיבא never said all the reddish shades combine either.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. It brings up a possible answer, usually so it can be rejected.
Just as
Itself. The case itself.

phrases.english: And if you will say
just as you heard it from him about a mixed mark,
so too you have heard it from him about pure white;
but about the mixed mark itself, did you hear it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא כִּי הֵיכִי דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ בְּפָתוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible defense of the Step 9 proof against Step 10, and then undermines it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Questions whether רבי עקיבא holds that all shades combine even in the reddish (פתוך) case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The defense assumes we know רבי עקיבא's view about פתוך, but that view is itself unclear.

steps.title: משנה in נגעים: רבי עקיבא's description of reddish shades
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי עקיבא describes the reddish version of בהרת and the reddish version of סיד. Both are like wine diluted in water, but the reddish בהרת is bright like snow and the reddish סיד is darker.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי עקיבא says, the reddish shade of this one and of that one is like wine mixed with water. Only, the one of בהרת is strong like snow, and the one of סיד is duller than it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its doubt from Step 11 with a משנה. In it, רבי עקיבא describes how the reddish shades look, and the picture does not match רבי חנינא's cups of milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חנינא's picture, the base (milk) is the same and only the amount of red changes from cup to cup. Here רבי עקיבא says the red in both shades is the same, 'like wine mixed with water'. The difference is in the white underneath: snow-bright for בהרת, duller for סיד. So even for פתוך, רבי עקיבא's own words do not match the cups-of-milk model.

keyTerms.meaning: Reddish
Wine diluted with water
Strong / bright
Dimmer / duller

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי חנינא is weakened twice. His comparison fits only reddish shades, and even for reddish shades רבי עקיבא's own description (the same red on a brighter or duller white) does not match the cups of milk.

phrases.english: But it was taught: רבי עקיבא says:
the reddish of this one and of that one
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the בהרת, and 'that one' is the lime-colored (סיד) mark.

phrases.english: is like wine mixed with water;
except that the one of בהרת is strong like snow,
and the one of lime is duller than it.

steps.raayaObject: That even for reddish (פתוך) shades, רבי עקיבא's view does not match רבי חנינא's cups-of-milk model.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נגעים 1:2, where רבי עקיבא says the reddish of בהרת and of סיד is the same 'wine mixed with water', differing only in how bright the white underneath is.
